figures.caption: Figure 1: Architecture of the proposed X-VAE. A pretrained autoencoder learns latent codes zAE; a K-component diagonal Gaussian mixture fit on these codes defines a fixed, data-driven prior p(z). The VAE encoder produces a per-coordinate posterior qϕ(z|x) and mixture responsibilities; each latent coordinate is formed by routed transport Equation (12)– Equation (13) and regularized toward p(z) by the mixture KL Equation (18).

Figure 2: Routed-transport sampling (one latent coordinate). The encoder produces percoordinate posterior parameters (ℓk, µ q k, σ q k). A component is routed from the frozen mixture, ck ∼ Cat(πp), and its noise ϵk is transported Equation (11) onto the posterior Gaussian to give zk, which is decoded. The responsibilities πq Equation (10) and the prior enter the mixture KL Equation (18) of the training objective Equation (17).

Figure 3: Architecture of the proposed X-VAE. Top: a deterministic autoencoder is trained first, and a K-component diagonal Gaussian mixture is fit once on its latent codes to give the fixed prior {πpk, µ p k, σ p k}Kk=1 (9), which is frozen during VAE training. Bottom: the VAE encoder emits a per-coordinate Gaussian posterior and routing weights (πqk, µ q k, σ q k); each latent coordinate is then formed by the routed-transport sampler—route a component c ∼ Cat(πq), draw ε ∼ N p(µpc , σ p c ), and transport it to zq = µqc + (σqc/σ p c ) ⊙ (ε − µpc) (13). Training combines the reconstruction MSE with the closed-form two-part mixture KL (18) (a categorical term plus a per-component Gaussian term). Dashed arrows mark the frozen prior parameters; solid arrows mark data flow.

Table 1: Final-epoch train/test objective with reconstruction and KL terms on MNIST and CelebA. Lowest test objective per dataset in bold; magnitudes are not comparable across datasets. For our routed-transport models the KL is the sum of a categorical and a percomponent Gaussian term (Equation (18)).

Table 2: Reconstruction error (MSE), FID, and Inception Score (IS) on MNIST and CelebA. Lower is better for MSE and FID, higher for IS; best per column in bold. We list the baselines and three of our strongest configurations; the complete per-model sweep is in Section I.

Table 4: Trainable parameter counts of the generative model. “Prior” isolates the parameters introduced specifically by the prior—VampPrior pseudo-inputs, the learned mixture parameters of the MoG/GM-VAE, and the hierarchical conditional-prior network, while X-VAE stores its prior in fixed buffers and so adds none. Counts include the shared convolutional backbone, which is identical across all models. X-VAE additionally pretrains an autoencoder (0.45M / 3.48M parameters on MNIST / CelebA), a one-time first stage not counted here. The GM-VAE’s large total comes from its per-component encoder heads, not from its prior.
